messages:
sam: Heads-up 1 Tangram's LoRA adapter landed under adapters/tangram and I kicked off a focused quickpack (tangram_micro_qp) to validate int4+row-sparsity. We're seeing a weird microtoken issue: commas and trailing cents dropped in large numbers (e.g. $1,200.50 -> \"1200\"). Anyone free to triage?

elaine: Oof. Can you paste a minimal repro snippet? Comma behavior sounds like tokenizer merge or postproc rounding.

sam: Repro below (intermittent on int4+row-sparse, fp16 ok):
```
Invoice:
- Order: #A-001, amount: $1,200.50
- Order: #A-002, amount: $45.75
Prompt: \"Return JSON with order_id (string) and amount (string)\"

Bad output: [{\"order_id\":\"A-001\",\"amount\":\"1200\"},{\"order_id\":\"A-002\",\"amount\":\"45\"}]
```
(the \",\" and decimals dropped)

dmitri: Quickpack stats I pulled: fp16 baseline cents/comma_preserve 0.05% failure, int8 0.4%, int4+row-sparse 3.2%. PPL rises moderately. Looks like quant + sparsity interaction causing low-prob microtoken collapse.

eval-bot: quickpack run qp-3667890123-1 complete. Deltas vs fp16: 
- comma+decimal preservation: +3.15% failure (int4+row-sparse)
- JSON validity: failures 0.4% -> 2.6%
- low-prob token drop: +2.9%

elaine: Two immediate checks: 1) does the Tangram adapter include any numeric normalizer (strip commas)? 2) token boundary for \",50\" or \".50\" 1 are those separate tokens or attached?

sam: Adapter had a legacy comma-stripper for internal search; I reverted that and re-ran: comma loss down to 2.1% but decimals still ~1.9%. So adapter helps but not whole root cause.

dmitri: Runtime note: row-sparsity uses per-row block reductions that can erase microtoken logits that sit on block edges. Experiments I recommend: (A) reduce sparsity fraction from 0.25 -> 0.12, (B) switch row->head-wise sparsity, (C) try asymmetric quant scales for int4. Also add 60 targeted cases into the quickpack focusing on thousands and cents.

eval-bot: queued ablation qp-3667890123-2: int4(row-sparse0.12) and qp-3667890123-3: int4(head-sparse).

elaine: Also run deterministic seed + warm vs cold KV cache; some quant kernels misbehave on early caching for low-prob tokens.

sam: Running ablation now. If int4(row0.12) doesn't reach parity we'll route Tangram -> int8-canary to avoid customer impact while we iterate.

dmitri: FYI I ran a quick local ablation: row0.12 -> comma+decimal drop ~1.1%, head-sparse -> 0.6%. Head-sparse looks promising.

eval-bot: ablation results attached: 
- int4(row0.12): ppl 1.23, comma_decimal_drop 1.08%, json_fail 1.05%
- int4(head-sparse): ppl 1.18, comma_decimal_drop 0.62%, json_fail 0.58%
- fp16 baseline: ppl 1.01, comma_decimal_drop 0.05%

elainE: (typo) Elaine here 1 head-sparse much closer. We should add the 60 targeted assertions and re-run head-sparse variant end-to-end before proposing a production path.

sam: I'll patch quickpack with 60 edge cases and run head-sparse + deterministic seeds. If stable, propose head-sparse int4 for Tangram; otherwise fall back to int8-canary.

dmitri: I'll prepare a minimal reproducer (6 failing examples + config) in case runtime needs a kernel bug. If we can reproduce deterministically, open a ticket with logs and model snapshot.

eval-bot: new run qp-3667890123-4 (head-sparse + 60 assertions) queued.

sam: Thanks everyone. Leaving routing override ready and will post final numbers when qp-4 finishes. If you see other microtoken oddities for Tangram, drop examples here. :eyes:
